To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a putative glucose and Galactose transporter gene from Brucella was identified by its complementation of two Escherichia Coli transport mutants, the gene is similar to fucP and hisG genes of E. Coli,

the glucose and galactoses transporter genes were isolated by functional complementaion of E. coli strains that lacked glucose or galactoses transporters, respectively, and that the gene product is a member of the major facilitators superfamily.
we have cloned the gene for a glucose/galactose transporter from B. abortus strain 23/08 and shown that it is a member of the major facilitation superfamily of transporters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the gene encoding a glucose and galactoses transporter from B. abortus 2308.
the isolation and characterization of the glucose and galactoses transport gene of Brucella aborts strain 2308.
the isolation, characterization, and sequencing of a gene from Brucella 2308 which encodes a glucose and galactoses transporter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gene cloned by complementation of E. coli strains deficient in galactose or glucose transport is a member of the major facilitators family of membrane proteins, and that the protein encoded by the ORF is the putative glucose and/or galactose transporter in B. abortus strain 23/18.

the gene for the putive transporter for glucose and lactose from B. abortus strain 23/8 was isolated by the functional complementation of E. coli strains lacking either the glucose or galactoase transport system.
the gene for a glucose/galactose transporter from B. abortus strain 23/8 has been identified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the B. abortus 2308 glucose and galactoses gene is similar to the fucP gene from E. coli and that the hisG gene is incomplete.
the glucose and galactoses transporters are encoded by the same gene.
the B. abortus 2308 gene encoding a glucose and galactoses transporter has been cloned, sequenced, and found to be a member of the major facilitation superfamily.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B. abortus glucose/galactose transporter is a member of the Major Facilitator Superfamily of transporters, which are characterized by the presence of 12 transmembrane segments.
the B. abortus glucose and galactoside transporter gene is a member of a new family of the major facilitators.
the gene for glucose and galacose uptake is present in the B. abortus genome and that it is a member of the major facilitation superfamily.
